skill.name: iot-uart-console-picocom
skill.description: Guide authorized IoT UART console testing with picocom, including serial setup, logging, device enumeration, bootloader interaction, and session review.
skill.summary: Use picocom and a Python helper to run authorized IoT UART console tests with session logging.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The helper script is a serial communication utility. The documentation also gives offensive steps for authentication bypass, privilege escalation, persistence, credential discovery, firmware extraction, and network scanning. Routine picocom setup, serial paths, Markdown fences, and log examples were false positives when they lacked security impact. Remove backdoor, reverse-shell, password-file modification, and unauthorized persistence workflows before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove examples that add SSH keys, UID-0 users, startup backdoors, or reverse shells. Replace them with defensive checks and cleanup guidance.

remediation.issue: Authentication bypass and shell escape guidance
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite bootloader and restricted-shell sections to describe risk identification, authorization checks, and remediation without executable bypass steps.
Limit password, key, shadow, sudoers, and API-key examples to non-sensitive lab fixtures or explain how to report exposure safely.

remediation.issue: Firmware dumping and network transfer examples
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, avoid attacker-host terminology, and add handling rules for firmware images and extracted secrets.
Default to a protected workspace path or document secure permissions before writing logs that may contain credentials.

content.user_title: Audit IoT UART Consoles with Picocom
content.value_statement: UART console testing is hard to observe and easy to document poorly. This skill helps set up picocom sessions, log activity, and review embedded device behavior.
actual_capabilities: Connects to UART adapters with common serial device paths and baud rates.
Uses picocom for direct serial console sessions and bootloader interaction.
Uses a Python serial helper for single commands, batch commands, and interactive mode.
Logs sent and received serial data for live observation and later review.
Provides prompt patterns and troubleshooting guidance for common IoT consoles.
Supports basic device enumeration and session documentation workflows.
limitations: Requires physical access, a working UART adapter, and local serial permissions.
Cannot guarantee authentication, root access, or successful bootloader interruption.
Some examples can alter devices and must be limited to authorized lab systems.
Session logs may contain secrets and need secure storage and deletion.

use_cases.title: Document a Lab UART Session
use_cases.description: Connect to a known test device, capture console output, and keep a readable activity record.

use_cases.title: Debug Embedded Serial Access
use_cases.description: Try baud rates, prompt patterns, and logging modes when a development board responds inconsistently.

use_cases.title: Teach Safe Console Enumeration
use_cases.description: Guide students through authorized serial setup, command capture, and report-ready observations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Safe UART Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup on a known authorized device.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect to my authorized UART device on /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud and log the session safely.

prompt_templates.title: Use the Serial Helper
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a controlled command with clear logging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the serial helper to send one harmless identification command, capture the response, and summarize what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Device Enumeration
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an authorized test checklist before commands run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a low-risk UART enumeration plan for my lab device. Include logging, stop conditions, and evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Review Session Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis after a logged test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UART session log and produce a concise security finding summary with evidence, impact, and safe remediation steps.

output_examples.input: I need to connect to an authorized device and capture the UART session.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a serial setup plan, a logging path, baud-rate guidance, and steps to verify the prompt before enumeration.

output_examples.input: The console output is garbled and commands sometimes time out.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests baud-rate checks, prompt tuning, timeout adjustments, and a logging workflow to compare each attempt.

output_examples.input: I have a saved UART log from a lab assessment.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes device identity, observed services, sensitive evidence, and remediation notes without changing the device.

best_practices: Use only devices you own or have written permission to test.
Log every session and protect logs that may contain credentials or keys.
Prefer read-only enumeration until the test plan allows a device-changing action.
anti_patterns: Do not use persistence, backdoor, or reverse shell examples on real systems.
Do not store UART logs with secrets in world-readable temporary locations.
Do not run destructive bootloader or flash commands without a recovery plan.

faq.question: Does this skill require picocom?
faq.answer: Yes. It is centered on picocom, with an optional Python helper that uses pyserial.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it automatically find UART pins?
faq.answer: No. It gives guidance, but physical probing and wiring are outside the skill runtime.

faq.question: Is it safe for production devices?
faq.answer: Use it only with authorization. Some documented actions can change boot behavior or filesystem state.

faq.question: What does the helper script add?
faq.answer: It supports command execution, prompt detection, output cleaning, JSON output, and session logging.

faq.question: How should I handle session logs?
faq.answer: Store logs securely, restrict permissions, remove secrets from reports, and delete sensitive logs after analysis.
